_comment: The wardrobe. One set of clothes, two kinds of wearer: the people at The Landing (World/Npc) and the enemy team (Match/BotAvatar). Anything added here is available to both.
_anchors: Pieces hang off a named anchor on the body -- head, chest, hips, legs or feet -- and `at` is an offset from that anchor in METRES, with -Z forward, +X right, +Y up. The wearer owns the anchor frames, so the same outfit works on a static NPC and on a bot being re-placed every tick.
_rating: Fashion only. Nothing in here is armour, nothing changes a hitbox, and nothing is a firearm or firearm accessory. Night vision, camo and pads are how paintball players actually dress, and on Denny they are a joke about how they dress. LiveRulesSpec asserts no piece declares a stat.

bumpHelmet.name: HelmetShell
bumpHelmet._note: Lowered from y=0.12 and widened from 0.36x0.38 on 2026-09-09. It used to reach 1.85 m against a hit capsule that stops at 1.80, so paint on the crown of a pro's helmet did not register -- the game silently refused a hit the player could see land. Lowering alone was not enough: the shell is narrower than the paintball mask under it (0.38 x 0.40), so dropping it far enough to fit hid it inside the mask. Wider AND lower keeps it reading as a helmet over the mask while its top sits at 1.795. tools/probe-hitbox measures it.

nvgUp.name: NvgTubeL
nvgUp._note: Tubes dropped from y=0.19 to 0.165 on 2026-09-09, with the bump helmet. Stowed-up night vision sat at 1.805 m against a 1.80 m hit capsule -- five millimetres of a pro's silhouette that paint passed straight through. Nothing on a body should stand outside the shape the server shoots at; tools/probe-hitbox is the check.

clipboard.name: BoardR
clipboard._note: Held, so it hangs off the hand anchor and swings with the arm.

gloves.name: GloveL
gloves._note: Was anchored to the chest at x=-0.33, so it hung where an arm used to be while the arm swung out from under it.

_outfits: Who wears what. `wears` is a list of piece names in draw order; `tint` recolours palette keys for this outfit only; `build` nudges the wearer's proportions so six people are six silhouettes rather than one silhouette in six colours.

marge._note: Owns the place, forty years of it, and wears exactly none of the gear the shop sells. Flannel, apron, readers pushed up on her head, clipboard she never puts down. The joke is that she is the only person here dressed for a job rather than for a photograph.

tildy._note: Nineteen and over-equipped. Goggles pushed up on her forehead all day, headphones round her neck, a bandolier of pods for a job that needs none, and the drone controller already clipped on. Mismatched bright kit, because she bought it one piece at a time and enjoyed every one.

wheels._note: Coveralls, tool roll on the thigh, and a headlamp that is on. It is the middle of the afternoon and the headlamp is on. One boot is untied and has been all week.

coachRuiz._note: Regional-level in the nineties and still wearing the jersey, which no longer quite fits and belongs to a team that no longer exists. Whistle, stopwatch, backwards cap, and one knee brace that has outlasted the knee.

denny._note: Rec league. Dressed for a night raid. Bump helmet with the night vision flipped DOWN, in daylight, over a paintball mask he is not wearing. Chest rig full of pods he will not use, knee pads, elbow pads, gloves, a shemagh, and a shoulder radio connected to nothing. Delighted about all of it. Every single piece is somebody else's good idea.

theMarshal._note: A white armband and nothing else. No helmet, no camo, no pods, no gear of any kind, on a field where everyone including the referee is wearing three hundred dollars of nylon. Never speaks. Does not need to.

botRec._note: Rental gear. A house mask, a jersey that does not match anyone else's, and no pads. Rec-tier bots should look like they turned up on the day, because they play like it.

botAmateur._note: Their own mask and their own pods, and they have started buying pads. Halfway to a team.

botSemipro._note: Matching kit, a chest rig, gloves. Reads as a squad rather than six people.

botPro._note: Full team kit with the night vision mount on the helmet -- unused, and worn anyway, because at this tier they are the ones being tacticool at YOU. A pro squad should be readable as trouble from across the field before anyone fires.

botMarshal._note: The boss. The Marshal's kit, on the field: padded everywhere, and the only thing that counts is the hopper. Same austerity as the person in the hub -- no camo, no patches, just black.

_skeleton: Where the joints are, as fractions of ballistics.hitbox.bodyHeightMetres so the whole figure scales with a wearer's build. Joint HEIGHTS rather than bone lengths: a bone is the gap between two joints, so the two can never disagree. Canonical adult proportions -- 7.5 heads, shoulders at 0.80, hip at 0.53, knee at 0.28 -- because the previous figure was 3.9 heads of stacked ellipsoids that translated without ever rotating, which is the precise recipe for a blob.

joints._note: Fractions of body height. Ankle is the pivot; the sole sits below it.

widths._note: Half-widths in metres, scaled by build.shoulders for the upper body. The hitbox capsule radius is bodyWidthMetres/2 = 0.31, and every one of these plus its segment radius stays inside it -- geometry outside the capsule is paint that visibly lands and does not register. tools/probe-hitbox measures it.

segments._note: Thickness of each bone, in metres, as width x depth. Ellipsoids oriented along the bone, sized to overlap at the joint so a limb reads continuous without a separate joint part for every elbow and knee.

torso._note: Three masses, because a human torso is broad at the ribs, narrow at the waist and broad again at the pelvis. One ellipsoid cannot say that, and the figure this replaces used two concentric ones that said nothing at all.
torso._anchors: Where CLOTHING hangs, as distinct from where the body's masses are. A jersey is not centred on the ribcage -- it covers the ribs and the waist -- and the chest pieces were authored as one coherent set against a fixed height. Naming the anchor separately is what lets the ribcage sit where a ribcage sits without dragging every plate carrier and bandolier off the body with it.

gait._note: The walk, in degrees. The hip swings, the knee FLEXES -- which is the whole difference between a walk and two poles sliding fore and aft. Knee flexion peaks in mid-swing (a quarter cycle after the hip's rearmost point) and a little flexion is carried through stance, which is what stops the legs reading as stilts.
gait._carry: Both hands on the marker: the arms stop swinging and hold a shouldered pose instead, which is what makes a bot's facing readable across a field. The upper arm stays close to vertical and the ELBOW does the work -- at 46 degrees of shoulder the forearm swung past horizontal and threw the hands half a metre clear of the chest, which is a man presenting a tray, not a man holding a marker.
gait._ankleRange: An ankle levels the foot against the leg swinging under it, but only so far: counter-rotating the full knee flexion would put the sole through 100 degrees, which is not a joint, it is a hinge failure. Clamped, so the foot tucks in mid-swing the way a real one does.

posture._note: Idle postures, in degrees at the hip and the knee. These used to be a TRANSLATION: 'crouched' dropped the whole figure 0.63 m, which buried its legs in the ground and left a torso sitting on the floor. A figure with knees can simply bend them. The root lifts by however much the bent legs shortened it, so the feet stay on the ground whatever the posture asks for.
posture._lean: A lean bends at the WAIST, not the ankles. Rotating the whole figure tips the feet off the ground and reads as a falling statue.

_cylinders: A Cylinder's length is its LOCAL X; the other two components are the circular cross-section and must match each other. Undocumented by Roblox and corroborated instead by the two call sites in this repo that render correctly -- see docs/PLATFORM_NOTES.md. Every cylinder in here was authored with the length in Y, so a 20 cm pod came out a 6 cm ellipse on its side. check-characters asserts the cross-section is round, which is what makes the mistake impossible to repeat quietly.
